acceptance: Each timing records the 5-minute load average at start, taken from make heavy-status, and is refused if it is above the CPU count.
The scale factor 1 run completes or its failure is explained; mcp-sf1-run-incomplete-without-error-20261114 is referenced.
The recommendation states whether any run exceeds Codex's 60 s default tool timeout, with the numbers.
The host-load smoke for PR #4203 is not repeated with real load; the unit tests that fake the sampler are cited as the evidence.
context:
Found during a retrospective on 2026-11-15. Guardrails: linked worktree, one PR; no live-cloud runs; heavy work only via lock-taking entry points; re-verify cited facts before acting.

Closeout (2026-11-15): measured on develop plus PR BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4251, through a real MCP stdio client (mcp 2.3.0, benchbox-mcp), run_benchmark platform=duckdb benchmark=tpch seed=1, default 3 iterations, under make heavy-run. 10-CPU host; load average at start of each call was 3.4 to 5.0 (1 minute) and 4.3 to 4.7 (5 minute), below the CPU count. Warm (data and database already present, data_generation NOT_RUN): SF 0.01 2.2 s then 1.0 s; SF 0.1 1.4 s, 1.4 s; SF 1 2.6 s, 2.6 s. Cold (empty BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR, so data is generated and loaded): SF 1 31.6 s, then 2.8 s warm; SF 0.1 15.4 s, then 1.7 s warm. Cold SF 0.01 was not measured. Every call returned mcp_metadata.status 'completed' with 66 of 66 queries passed, including all four SF 1 calls; the 'incomplete' result recorded in mcp-sf1-run-incomplete-without-error-20261114 did not reproduce. Against Codex's 60 s default tool timeout: no measured call exceeds it; the slowest, cold SF 1, uses about half. Recommendation, replacing the earlier one: no local job tools are needed for TPC-H on DuckDB up to SF 1. Not measured, so not covered: scale factors above 1, other benchmarks and slower platforms, where a cold first call could pass 60 s. The host-load smoke for PR #4203 was not repeated with real load; its evidence is the unit tests that fake the sampler.
description:
Problem: mcp-local-run-timeout-measure-20261113 was closed on timings measured while 20 leaked spin loops held the host at load 60 to 80 (a heavy-work guard gap fixed in PR #4236). Its 6 to 14 second figures and its recommendation (no local job tools; document a limit) rest on invalid numbers. The same window also invalidates the quiet and loaded host-load smoke for bundle-record-host-load-20261113.

Outcome: valid timings for TPC-H on DuckDB through a real MCP stdio client at scale factors 0.01, 0.1 and 1, taken when make heavy-status shows a 5-minute load average below the CPU count, and a recommendation that replaces the earlier one.
